current_example.title: Example: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation

q-78549.name: Question 1
q-78549.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+4z=-2 \\ x+3y+9z=0 \\ y+6z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
q-78549.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 & 6 \\ -6 & 6 & -5 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=0,y=-3,z=1.$

Finally, $x+y+z=0+(-3)+1=-2.$

q-78553.name: Question 2
q-78553.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x+2y+z=3 \\ x-2y+z=1 \\ 2x-y+2z=5\end{aligned}
$$

The system above has the matrix representation $Ax=b.$ Given that $x=⟨x,y,z⟩$ is unique, what is the value of $x+y+z?$ 

*Hint: The inverse of the coefficient matrix is given by*

$$
\,{A}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$
q-78553.worked_solution:
First, let's write our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =b \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solution is $x=-1,y=1,z=4.$

Finally, $x+y+z=-1+1+4=4.$

q-104515.name: Question 3
q-104515.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z=-1 \\ 3x-z=5+3y \\ 3z-2y=6-x\end{aligned}
$$

Find  $x+y+z.$
q-104515.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the system in the correct order:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+y-2z=-1 \\ 3x-3y-z=5 \\ x-2y+3z=6\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we  write the system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|+(-2)|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-9-2)-(9+1)-2(-6+3) \\  & =-22-10+6 \\  & =-26.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}3 & -3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-11 & 10 & -3 \\ -1 & 8 & -5 \\ -7 & 4 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-11 & -10 & -3 \\ 1 & 8 & 5 \\ -7 & -4 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-11 & 1 & -7 \\ -10 & 8 & -4 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}-11 & 1 & -7 \\ -10 & 8 & -4 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the solution to the given system is

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}-11 & 1 & -7 \\ -10 & 8 & -4 \\ -3 & 5 & -9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{26}[\begin{aligned}-26 \\ 26 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x+y+z=1-1+1=1.$

q-10100.name: Question 4
q-10100.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}2x+3y+z=6 \\ 4x+7y+2z=0 \\ 3x+y+z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
q-10100.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 4 & 7 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-3|\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(7-2)-3(-2)+1(4-21) \\  & =10+6-17 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}4 & 7 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 4 & 7\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & -17 \\ 2 & -1 & -7 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -17 \\ -2 & -1 & 7 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -17 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=-\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ -17 & 7 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 17 & -7 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 17 & -7 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-29 \\ -12 \\ 100\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-29,y=-12,z=100.$

q-10100.html:
Question 4
?

Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix: {2x+3y+z=64x+7y+2z=03x+y+z=1

a
x=29,y=12,z=100
b
x=−29,y=−12,z=−100
c
x=−25,y=−12,z=100
d
x=−29,y=−15,z=100
e
x=−29,y=−12,z=100
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We wish to write this system in the form Ax=b, where A is a 3×3 matrix and x and b are 3×1 column vectors. We can do this as follows: [231472311][xyz]=[601].

Now, the solution to Ax=b is given by x=A−1b. So, we compute A−1 as follows:

Step 1:

det(A)=|231472311|=2|7211|−3|4231|+1|4731|=2(7−2)−3(−2)+1(4−21)=10+6−17=−1.

Step 2:

M=[|7211||4231||4731||3111||2131||2331||3172||2142||2347|]=[5−2−172−1−7−102].

Step 3:

C=[52−17−2−17−102].

Step 4:

CT=[5−2−12−10−1772].

Step 5:

A−1=1det(A)CT=−11[5−2−12−10−1772]=[−521−21017−7−2].

Hence x=A−1b=[−521−21017−7−2][601]=[−29−12100]. Hence the solution is x=−29,y=−12,z=100.

q-78561.name: Question 5
q-78561.problem:
Consider a system of $n$ linear equations in $n$ variables, written in matrix form as $D\,t=q.$ Here, $D$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $t$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $q$ is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,t & =q \\ \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\color{blue}{\phantom{{D}^{-1}}}}D\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ {I}_{n}\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,\bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\color{blue}{\phantom{\mathbf{q}}}} \\ t & ={D}^{-1}\,q\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom and left to right, what are the missing parts of the derivation?
q-78561.worked_solution:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,t=q$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,t & =q \\ {D}^{-1}D\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ {I}_{n}\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ t & ={D}^{-1}\,q\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and $q.$

q-78565.name: Question 6
q-78565.problem: Consider a matrix equation $B\,x=A\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\times 2$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $2\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
q-78565.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${B}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,x=A\,d$ by ${B}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & =A\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d \\ {I}_{2}\,x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d.\end{aligned}

q-78565.html:
Question 6
?

Consider a matrix equation Bx=Ad, where A and B are 2×2 non-singular matrices, while x and d are 2×1 column vectors. Solve the equation for x.

a
x=BAd
b
x=B−1Ad
c
x=AdB−1
d
x=AB−1d
e
x=AdB
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since B is not singular, it must have an inverse B−1. Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation Bx=Ad by B−1, we obtain

Bx=AdB−1Bx=B−1AdI2x=B−1Adx=B−1Ad.
